diagnostic_evidence.quote: In particular, we approximate the minimizer of a convex minimization problem over the space $V \coloneqq W^{1,1}_0(\Omega)$.

issues.failure_explanation: Finite energy gives the flux the integrability needed to pair with gradients in the natural energy space, not arbitrary L^1 gradients. Already for the quadratic energy, on a corner of angle 3π/2 a cutoff of r^{2/3} sin(2θ/3) is a zero-boundary solution with bounded load. A similarly cut off test function r^{-β} sin(2θ/3), with 2/3 ≤ β < 1, belongs to W^{1,1}_0, but its gradient product with the solution gradient is not integrable. Thus the asserted equality can have an undefined left-hand side.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the weak formulation to zero-trace test functions with finite φ-energy, while retaining the extended-valued minimization over W^{1,1}_0.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed equivalence with a variational equation on all of V is invalid. The minimization formulation and the later uses of finite-energy test functions need not be abandoned.
issues.title: The weak formulation is not defined for every W^{1,1} test function
issues.why_classification: This is a standard local correction of the test space and preserves the minimizer, finite element methods, and advertised approximation regimes.

issues.failure_explanation: The convex function inside the integral depends on x through |∇u(x)|, so averaging its argument does not give the asserted Jensen bound. For φ(t)=t^{10}/10, let a scalar gradient G equal 0 and 1 on equal portions of an element and take χ=1. Then the integral of φ_{|G|}(|G-χ|), normalized by element volume, is 1/20, whereas that of φ_{|G|}(|average(G-χ)|) is 1/16+1/20480, which is larger. Smooth approximations preserve the strict failure.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: On each element, use a constant comparison vector χ and the fixed shift |χ|. Apply the triangle inequality in F-space and Jensen's inequality to φ_{|χ|}; Proposition prop:Distances then gives the same best-approximation conclusion.
issues.overall_effect: The interpolation estimate used to obtain both localized a priori bounds is not established by the displayed argument.
issues.title: Jensen's inequality is applied with a spatially varying shift
issues.why_classification: A short local replacement using properties already supplied proves the same estimate, with no loss of scope or rate.

issues.failure_explanation: The nodal midrange argument applies only at interior vertices; the companion instead sets boundary vertices to zero. On a square split by one diagonal, assign alternating values 1,-1,1,-1 to the boundary vertices and interpolate affinely on both triangles. This is a CR function with zero boundary-face means and is continuous across the diagonal, so every interior tangential jump vanishes. There are no interior vertices, hence its companion is zero. The left-hand side is positive while the stated right-hand side is zero.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Include boundary faces with one-sided tangential traces, prove the boundary-vertex estimate using the zero face mean, and carry those contributions through the one-sided versions of the subsequent bubble estimates.
issues.overall_effect: The local companion estimate is false on admissible meshes, and the subsequent companion-based proofs lack boundary control.
issues.title: The companion estimate omits necessary boundary-face contributions
issues.why_classification: The asserted jump bound must be weakened and a boundary version of the companion argument supplied. This is a contained repair that can preserve the final approximation regimes.

issues.failure_explanation: Changing shifts determined by v_h produces costs involving jumps of F(∇_h v_h), not jumps of ∇_h e_h. Likewise, the displayed conjugacy equivalence requires a shift based on an input gradient of e_h. The resulting assertion is false: on a regular fan around an interior vertex, choose CR face basis functions e and w with disjoint element supports but that common vertex. Set v_h=Mw, u_h=Mw-e, and v=0. For φ(t)=t^p/p with p>2, the right-hand side of eq:Enrichment2 is independent of M. However, E e is nonzero on the support of w, where e=0, so the left-hand side grows like M^{p-2}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain the stated approximation bound only for the aligned case e_h=v_h. For general errors, establish a replacement bound by the natural error energy plus the face sum of h_γ times the squared L^2 jump of F(∇_h v_h). The paper's two-case residual arguments can then control this additional sum before absorption in the main proof.
issues.overall_effect: The weighted absorption used in the main medius proof is unsupported. The interpolation application with u_h=0 has aligned shifts and is not defeated by this particular defect.
issues.title: The weighted companion bound uses shifts unrelated to the error gradients
issues.why_classification: A genuinely different weighted companion estimate and a reorganization of the absorption are required, but the supplied shift-change and two-case machinery support a contained repair without sacrificing the main approximation rates.

issues.failure_explanation: For arbitrary W^{1,1} functions, A(∇v) need not even be locally integrable. Even with bounded gradients, its divergence need not be a function: for the quadratic energy and a non-affine conforming piecewise-affine v, it contains face measures. Applying an N-function pointwise to the absolute value of that distribution and integrating against dx is undefined. Allowing an integral to be infinite does not itself define it for a distributional input.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Specify that the residual is defined only when the flux has a measurable divergence, and explicitly assign the residual value infinity outside that domain; alternatively, state the needed flux and divergence hypotheses.
issues.overall_effect: The arbitrary-v companion and interpolation assertions are not well-defined as stated. Applications to v=0 or to the solution with divergence equal to the bounded load do not have this defect.
issues.title: The divergence residual is undefined for the quantified class of functions
issues.why_classification: An explicit extended-value convention or standard domain restriction resolves the problem without altering any finite residual estimate or application to the stated PDE solutions.

issues.failure_explanation: The companion lemma supplies a conjugate shifted N-function of the divergence residual. The interpolation theorem and its proof instead use the primal shifted function, and the conforming proof subsequently applies the oscillation lemma to that primal term. No uniform comparison justifies these replacements. For φ(t)=t^p/p and sufficiently small s, φ_a(s)=a^{p-2}s^2/2 whereas (φ_a)^*(s)=a^{2-p}s^2/2; their ratio is unbounded as a varies when p≠2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the interpolation residual with (φ_{|∇v|})^*, carry that conjugate consistently through the conforming proof, and use the dual shift-change estimate before applying the oscillation lemma.
issues.overall_effect: The stated interpolation residual has unsupported nonlinear scaling, and the displayed elimination of the residual in the conforming a priori proof is invalid.
issues.title: The interpolation theorem replaces the conjugate residual by the primal N-function
issues.why_classification: The repair changes a substantive term of the interpolation theorem, potentially by an unbounded factor. It nevertheless leaves the advertised conforming a priori conclusion accessible using the existing lemmas.

issues.failure_explanation: Both indicators require evaluating energies at u_h, the exact unregularized discrete minimizer that the iteration is intended to compute. The supplied iterate u_{h,n} and iteration-error bound do not provide these values. Consequently, the comparisons selecting the next adaptive action cannot be performed from the stated available quantities.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must replace the exact-solution energy values by computable regularization indicators and establish their intended interpretation in both exponent regimes.
issues.overall_effect: The adaptive procedure is not executable as described, so its parameter-selection mechanism is not supplied by the paper.
issues.title: Adaptive regularization decisions require the unknown exact discrete solution
issues.why_classification: The source supplies no validated computable replacement for the quantities driving its adaptive decisions. Replacing them changes the procedure rather than merely completing routine algebra.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Moreover, the minimizer $u\in W^{1,p}_0(\Omega)$ to \eqref{eq:MinProb} and any $v\in W^{1,p}_0(\Omega)$ satisfy

issues.failure_explanation: A CR function is not an admissible competitor in the continuous minimization, so this energy gap can be negative even with zero oscillation. For p=2 and f=1, take the diamond with vertices (±1,0),(0,±3), split along its horizontal diagonal. Its CR space is spanned by w=1-2|y|/3, and the discrete minimum energy is -3/4. For every conforming zero-trace v, integration by parts gives (1,v)=((-x,0),∇v); completing the square and using ∫Ω x²=1 gives J(v)≥-1/2. Thus the displayed left-hand side at the exact CR solution is at most -1/4, while a squared estimator is nonnegative.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict this energy-gap equivalence to conforming iterates and remove the CR error-control claim. Retaining a CR guarantee requires a nonnegative nonconforming error measure and a justified estimator, including the necessary nonconformity contributions.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted two-sided residual-estimator guarantee is false for the CR method, including exact discrete iterates and constant data.
issues.title: A nonconforming energy gap is incorrectly asserted to be a nonnegative error measure
issues.why_classification: The source-supported restriction removes the guarantee for the paper's principal nonconforming method. A comparable CR guarantee requires an additional estimator and reliability/efficiency theory not established here.
